title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-throughput-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: customers running Dedicated fleets need clearer end-to-end visibility into burst capacity consumption, effective throughput guarantees, and the token-bucket behavior that controls bursts. This PR implements enhanced reporting and instrumentation for the Dedicated autoscaler to make burst consumption and throughput guarantees observable in the Console and via metrics.

What this change does: added token-bucket and burst-window metrics, per-fleet throughput SLA counters, and a compact utilization summary that correlates burst credits used with realized throughput. Also added a reporting endpoint used by the Console and extended the autoscaler's internal simulation tests to validate smoothing behavior under synthetic workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics: token_bucket_capacity, token_bucket_tokens, burst_window_used_tokens, burst_window_capacity, fleet_throughput_sla, fleet_throughput_actual
- [x] Exporters: Prometheus scraping + Grafana dashboard templates
- [x] Console: new per-fleet burst/throughput section (read-only) wired to reporting endpoint
- [x] Tests: unit tests for token-bucket accounting, integration test that replays traces against the autoscaler simulator
- [x] Docs: runtime/observability docs updated with metrics and dashboard screenshots

Migration/compatibility: All new metrics are additive. The reporting endpoint defaults to disabled; Console enables it via an opt-in feature flag for managed Dedicated accounts. No breaking changes to autoscaling decisions.

Performance: instrumentation is lightweight (atomic counters + buffered histogram flushes) and toggled behind config to avoid any CPU overhead for customers who do not opt in.

Related: ENG-3245 (design), ENG-4110 (Console integration), SUP-789 (customer support ticket that triggered visibility work).
